extracted.intended_audience: Users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (research mathematicians, computational algebraists, and advanced users implementing invariant-ring and polynomial-solving workflows)
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation of SINGULAR library procedures (usage, assumptions, return values, notes, and examples) for computing invariant rings, images of varieties/groups, stratifications, and solving polynomial systems over fields. Focused on how to call and interpret each procedure in various libraries (finvar, ainvar, rinvar, stratify, ffsolve, presolve).

rubrics_metrics.name: image_of_variety
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: image_of_variety(I,F); I: an arbitrary <ideal>, F: a 1xm <matrix> defining an invariant ring of some matrix group. Return: The <ideal> defining the image under that group of the variety defined by I. rel orbit variety(I,F) is called and the newly introduced variables in the output are replaced by the generators of the invariant ring. This ideal in the original variables defines the image of the variety defined by I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure from library finvar.lib. Example given: LIB "finvar.lib"; ring R=0,(x,y,z),dp; matrix F[1][3]=x+y+z,xy+xz+yz,xyz; ideal I=xy; print(image_of_variety(I,F)); -> xyz

rubrics_metrics.name: invariantRing (ainvar.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: invariantRing(m,p,q,b[,r,pa]); m matrix, p,q poly, b,r int, pa string. Returns an ideal containing generators of the ring of invariants of the additive group (K,+) given by the vector field m = sum m[i,1]*d/dx(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If b>0 stop after invariants of degree <= b (and at least one higher degree) are found; if b<=0 compute until all generators (use only if finitely generated). r=1 uses different reduction (sometimes faster). pa pauses whenever new invariants are found. Algorithm works in char 0 or sufficiently large characteristic. Examples show computing full invariant rings and computing invariants up to degree 6; warnings about non-finitely generated rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: derivate
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: derivate(m,id); m matrix, id poly/vector/ideal. Applies the vector field given by m componentwise to id.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vector field is m[1,1]*d/dx(1) + ... + m[n,1]*d/dx(n). Returns same type as input (poly/vector/ideal). Examples show results on polynomials, vectors, and ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: actionIsProper
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: actionIsProper(m); m matrix. Return: int = 1 if the action defined by m is proper, 0 if not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interprets m as vector field whose exponential defines the group action. Examples show returns 0 or 1 for given m's.

rubrics_metrics.name: reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: reduction(p,I[,q,n]); p poly, I ideal, [q monomial, n int]. Return: a polynomial equal to p - H(f1,...,fr) if LT(p) = H(LT(f1),...,LT(fr)); if q given compute maximal a with q^a dividing p-H(...) then return (p-H(...))/q^a; return p if no H found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a kind of SAGBI reduction in the subalgebra K[f1,...,fr]. n=1 chooses a different algorithm (sometimes faster). Example demonstrates usage with optional q to further divide.

rubrics_metrics.name: completeReduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: completeReduction(p,I[,q,n]); p poly, I ideal, [q monomial, n int]. Return: the SAGBI reduction of p with respect to I via 'reduction' as long as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: n=1 chooses alternate algorithm. Note suggests 'help reduction' for explanation. Examples show complete reduction returning 0 in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: localInvar
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: localInvar(m,p,q,h); m matrix, p,q,h polynomials. Assume: m(q) and h are invariant under the vector field m, h must be a ring variable. Return: a polynomial—the invariant polynomial of m with respect to p,q,h defined via a specific series formula and divided by h as often as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition: set inv = p if p invariant, else inv = m(q)^N * sum_{i=1..N-1} (-1)^i*(1/i!)*m^i(p)*(q/m(q))^i where m^N(p)=0, m^{N-1}(p) != 0. Example: localInvar returns -1/2*y^2 + xz.

rubrics_metrics.name: furtherInvar
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: furtherInvar(m,id,karl,q); m matrix, id,karl ideals, q poly. Assume: karl,id,q invariant under m and q must be a variable. Return: list of two ideals: first contains further invariants divisible by q and divided by q as often as possible; second contains all invariants given before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If n=1 alternate algorithm used. Example shows returned ideals and listed invariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: sortier
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sortier(id); id ideal/module. Return: the same ideal/module but with generators ordered by their leading terms, starting with the smallest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates generator reordering from arbitrary order to ordered by LT.

rubrics_metrics.name: HilbertSeries
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: HilbertSeries(I, w); ideal I, intvec wt. Purpose: compute the polynomial p of the Hilbert Series, represented by p/q, of the ring K[t1,...,tm,y1,...,yr]/I1 where 'w' are the weights and I1 is of the form I[1]-y1,...,I[r]-yr and is quasihomogeneous w.r.t. 'w'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: intvec. Note: leading 0 of result does not belong to p but is needed in Hilbert-driven std.

rubrics_metrics.name: HilbertWeights
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: compute the weights of the 'slack' variables needed for computing algebraic relations of the generators of I such that the Hilbert-driven 'std' can be used. Return: intvec. Assume: basering = K[t1,...,tm,...], I quasihomogeneous w.r.t. 'w' and contains only polynomials in t1,...,tm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used prior to HilbertSeries computations to determine weights.

rubrics_metrics.name: ImageVariety
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ImageVariety(ideal I, F [, w]); I ideal; F is a list/ideal, intvec w. Purpose: compute the Zariski closure of the image of the variety of I under the morphism F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If I and F are quasihomogeneous w.r.t. w then Hilbert-driven 'std' used. Returns a polynomial ring containing the ideal 'imageid' with variables Y(1)...Y(k). Examples show creation of new ring and accessing 'imageid' generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: ImageGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ImageGroup(G, action); ideal G, action. Purpose: compute the ideal of the image of G in GL(m,K) induced by the linear action 'action', where G is an algebraic group and 'action' defines an action of G on K^m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return is a polynomial ring with ideals 'groupid' (ideal of image of G) and 'actionid' (defines linear action of 'groupid' on K^m). Notes: variables giving only 0s in matrices are omitted. Example demonstrates resulting 'groupid' and 'actionid'.

rubrics_metrics.name: InvariantRing (rinvar.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: InvariantRing(G, Gact [, opt]); ideal G, Gact; int opt. Purpose: compute generators of the invariant ring of G w.r.t. action 'Gact'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume G finite and Gact linear. Return: ring R with ideals 'invars' (algebra generators), 'groupid' (ideal of G in new ring), and poly 'newA' (new representation of primitive root). Note: minimal polynomial of output may depend on random choices. Example shows accessing 'invars'.

rubrics_metrics.name: InvariantQ
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: InvariantQ(f, G, action); poly f; ideal G, action. Purpose: check whether polynomial f is invariant w.r.t. G acting via 'action'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering K[s1..,t1..] etc. Return: int 0 if not invariant, 1 if invariant. Note: G need not be finite. Designed to test invariance.

rubrics_metrics.name: LinearizeAction
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: LinearizeAction(G,action,r); ideal G, action; int r. Purpose: linearize the group action 'action' and find an equivariant embedding of K^m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume G contains only variables var(1..r); basering = K[s(1..r),t(1..m)], K = Q or Q(a) and minpoly != 0. Return: polynomial ring containing ideals 'actionid' (linearized action), 'embedid' (parameterization of equivariant embedding), 'groupid' (ideal of G in new ring). set printlevel>0 to see trace. Example demonstrates creation of new ring and checking LinearActionQ on actionid.

rubrics_metrics.name: LinearActionQ
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: LinearActionQ(action,nrs); ideal action, int nrs. Purpose: check whether the action defined by 'action' is linear w.r.t. specified variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: 0 action not linear, 1 action is linear. Example shows checking linearity for given action and different nrs values.

rubrics_metrics.name: LinearCombinationQ
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: LinearCombination(I, f); ideal I, poly f. Purpose: test whether f can be written as a linear combination of the generators of I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: 0 if f is not a linear combination, 1 if it is.

rubrics_metrics.name: MinimalDecomposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: MinimalDecomposition(f,a,b); poly f; int a, b. Purpose: decompose f = sum M[1,i]*M[2,i] where M[1,i] uses only s(1..a) and M[2,i] uses only t(1..b) so that r is minimal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume f in K[s(1..a),t(1..b)], K=Q or Q(a) and minpoly != 0. Return: 2 x r matrix M with decomposition. Example shows returned M and verification M[1,1]*M[2,1]+... - h = 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: NullCone
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: NullCone(G, action); ideal G, action. Purpose: compute the ideal of the nullcone of the linear action of G on K^n using Derksen’s algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering = K[s(1..r),t(1..n)], K = Q or Q(a) and minpoly != 0; G ideal of a reductive algebraic group in K[s(1..r)]; action linear. Return: ideal of nullcone. Note: generators are homogeneous but not necessarily invariant. Example lists returned generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: ReynoldsImage
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ReynoldsImage(RO, f); list RO, poly f. Purpose: compute the Reynolds image of polynomial f, where RO represents the Reynolds operator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: poly. Used in invariant computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: ReynoldsOperator
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ReynoldsOperator(G, action [, opt]); ideal G, action; int opt. Purpose: compute the Reynolds operator of group G acting via 'action'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: polynomial ring R over a simple extension of ground field containing list 'ROelements', ideals 'id','actionid' and polynomial 'newA'. ROelements are ideals representing substitution maps F:R->R according to zero-set of G. Assumes basering = K[s(1..r),t(1..n)], K = Q or Q(a') and minpoly != 0, G ideal of finite group in K[s(1..r)], action linear. Example usage context described.

rubrics_metrics.name: SimplifyIdeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: simplify ideal I to ideal I' without changing names of first m variables; new ideal I' might contain fewer variables and will contain variables var(1..m). Return: list [I', phi_map_ideal, list_of_variables, elimpart_list].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simplifies ideal while preserving first m variable names. Useful to reduce complexity of ideals for further processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: prepMat
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: prepMat(M,wr,ws,step); M matrix, wr intvec size ncols(M), ws intvec size nrows(M), step integer. Return: 2 lists of submatrices corresponding to filtrations specified by wr and ws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: entries M_ij = delta_i(x_j). wr determines which dx_i generate AdF^l(A) (columns appear from k-th submatrix if (k-1)*step <= wr[i] < k*step). ws determines which delta_i generate Z^l(L) (rows appear up to (k-1)-th). Entries of wr, ws, and step should be positive integers. Example demonstrates returned lists of submatrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: stratify
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: stratify(M,wr,ws,step); M matrix, wr intvec size ncols(M), ws intvec size nrows(M), step integer. Return: list of lists; each big-list entry corresponds to one locally closed set and contains: (1) intvec giving rs-vector, (2) ideal determining closed set, (3) list d of polynomials determining open set D(d[1]) or empty list if >1 open set, (4-n) lists of polynomials determining open sets leading to same rs-vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: ring ordering should be global (polynomial ring). M entries M_ij = delta_i(x_j). wr and ws used similarly to prepMat (with slightly different inequalities). Filtrations must be known; no sanity checks performed. Example shows output format and some sample local sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: ffsolve
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ffsolve(I[, L]); I ideal, L list of strings. Return: list L — the common roots of I as ideal. Assume basering is a finite field of type (p^n,a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library ffsolve.lib for multivariate equation solving over finite fields. Example demonstrates returned root lists with variable substitutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PEsolve
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: PEsolve(I[, i]); I ideal, i optional integer. Solve I over finite field using an equivalence property when i is not given or set to 2; if i=0 then only check whether common roots exist (return 1 if yes, 0 if no).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is finite field (p^n,a). Return: list when parameter omitted or set to 2; integer when parameter set to 0. Examples show verbose internal redefinitions and returned solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: simplesolver
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: simplesolver(I); I ideal. Solve I over finite field by exhaustive search. Return: list L, the common roots of I as ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is finite field (p^n,a). Example shows search-based solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: GBsolve
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: GBsolve(I); I ideal. Solve I over an extension of Z/p by Gröbner basis methods. Return: list L of common roots as ideals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is finite field (p^n,a). Example shows returned solutions similar to other ff solvers.

rubrics_metrics.name: XLsolve
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: XLsolve(I[, d]); I ideal, d optional integer. Solve system by a variant of the linearization technique, multiplying polynomials with monomials of degree at most d (default d=2). Return: list L of common roots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is finite field (p^n,a). Example demonstrates using XLsolve(I,3) to get solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: ZZsolve
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ZZsolve(I); I ideal. Solve I by mapping polynomials to a single univariate polynomial over an extension of the basering. Return: list of common roots as ideals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is finite field (p^n,a). Example shows returned root lists similar to other ff solvers.

rubrics_metrics.name: degreepart
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: degreepart(id,d1,d2[,v]); id ideal/module/other, d1,d2 integers, v intvec optional. Return: list of size 2: [1] generators of id of [v-weighted] total degree >= d1 and <= d2 (default v=1,...,1), [2] remaining generators of id.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Converts id to ideal if necessary; if id is a matrix/module then computes corresponding generators. Examples show extraction of degree-bounded parts and usage on modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: elimlinearpart
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: elimlinearpart(i[,n]); i ideal, n integer (default n = nvars(basering)). Return: list L with 5 entries: L[1] ideal after substituting from first n variables those appearing linearly (triangular form), L[2] ideal of substituted variables, L[3] ideal whose j-th element defines substitution of j-th var in L[2], L[4] ideal of basering variables with eliminated ones set to 0, L[5] ideal describing map from basering to itself so that L[1] is image of i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure interreduces internally w.r.t ordering dp. Useful to substitute/eliminate variables appearing linearly. Example demonstrates returned substitution ideals and maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: elimpart
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: elimpart(i [,n,e] ); i ideal, n,e integers (default n = nvars(basering), e = 1). Behavior: if e=0 substitute from linear part (like elimlinearpart); if e!=0 also eliminate by direct substitution. Return: list of 5 objects similar to elimlinearpart describing substituted ideal, substituted variables, substitutions, variables set to 0, and induced map. The ideal i is generated by [1] and [3] and map induces isomorphism k[x]/i -> k[..vars..]/[1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: applying to interred(i) may result in more substitutions but interred may be expensive for big ideals. Extensive examples given showing different outputs depending on parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: elimpartanyr
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: elimpartanyr(i [,p,e] ); i ideal, p polynomial (product of vars to be eliminated), e integer (default p=product of all vars, e=1). Return: list of 6 objects: [1] (interreduced) ideal after substituting vars appearing in p, [2] ideal of substituted variables, [3] substitutions, [4] ideal of variables of basering with substituted ones set to 0, [5] ideal describing the induced map where [1] is image, [6] int number of vars considered for substitution (#factors of p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure uses execute to create ring with ordering dp and applies elimpart. Example shows using elimpartanyr(i,z) and returns resulting ideals and count.
